extracted.intended_audience: organizers/advertisers of mathematical meetings and conferences preparing announcement submissions for the Notices of the American Mathematical Society
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting meeting/conference announcements to the Notices of the AMS, specifying required content, lead times, formatting/marking conventions, and publication scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and core content for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: AN ANNOUNCEMENT will be published in the Notices if it contains a call for papers, and specifies the place, date, subject (when applicable), and the speakers; a second announcement will be published only if there are changes or necessary additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include: explicit call for papers (when applicable), place, date, subject (if applicable), and speakers. The Notices will publish a second announcement only when there are changes or necessary additional information. Once an announcement has appeared, the event will be briefly noted in each issue until it has been held, with a parenthetical reference to the month, year, and page where the complete information first appeared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard fields included for North American meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: IN GENERAL, announcements of meetings and conferences held in North America carry only date, title of meeting, place of meeting, names of speakers (or sometimes a general statement on the program), deadlines for abstracts or contributed papers, and source of further information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For North American events, keep listings concise: include date, title, venue, speaker names or a short program statement, abstract/contributed-paper deadlines, and a contact/source for further information. Meetings outside North America may include more detailed information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended additional sections/fields for announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical informational headings shown in examples: ORGANIZING COMMITTEE, CONFERENCE TOPICS, INVITED SPEAKERS, PROGRAM, FUNDING, CALL FOR PAPERS, INFORMATION (contact details).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate (especially for non‑North American or larger events), include organizing committee, specific conference topics, invited speakers list, short program description, funding information/eligibility, call-for-papers instructions, submission deadlines, and complete contact information (postal address, phone/fax, email). The page provides many concrete examples of these fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application/participation-deadline notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In any case, if there is any application deadline with respect to participation in the meeting, this fact should be noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state any application or participation deadlines (not just abstract deadlines). Prominently record deadlines so potential participants can act on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission lead time and deadlines for listings
rubrics_metrics.description: DEADLINES for entries in this section are listed on the inside front cover of each issue. ... listings should be received in Providence SIX MONTHS prior to the scheduled date of the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers are urged to submit information early enough to allow the listing to appear in more than one issue to help participants arrange travel — send listings at least six months before the meeting date (and observe the issue-specific deadlines printed on the inside front cover).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication scope and timing policy (12‑month policy & September complete list)
rubrics_metrics.description: EFFECTIVE with the 1990 volume of the Notices, the complete list of Mathematical Sciences Meetings and Conferences will be published only in the September issue. In all other issues, only meetings and conferences for the twelve-month period following the month of that issue will appear. As new information is received for meetings and conferences that will occur later than the twelve-month period, it will be announced at the end of the listing in the next possible issue. That information will not be repeated until the date of the meeting or conference falls within the twelve-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the Notices' publication window: outside the September complete list, only events within the next 12 months from the issue date are printed. Information about events beyond that window may be listed briefly at the end of the listing in the next possible issue but will not be repeated until the event falls within the 12‑month window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking new or revised information
rubrics_metrics.description: Asterisks (*) mark those announcements containing new or revised information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an asterisk to indicate announcements that contain new or revised information; readers will see these flagged items in the listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to send announcements and contact for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: All communications on meetings and conferences in the mathematical sciences should be sent to the Editor of the Notices, care of the American Mathematical Society in Providence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send submissions/communications to the Notices' Editor (AMS, Providence) and follow the issue-specific deadlines listed on the inside front cover. Example announcement entries include full contact details (name, postal address, phone, fax, and email) for the event contact; include such details in your submission.
